implementation_notes: Export retains its exact public function type and delegates to ExportLimit with limit zero.
ExportLimit rejects negative limits before I/O, accepts zero as unlimited, and returns after the requested positive record count without another scan.
The writer is closed once in a deferred finalizer. A sole work or close error is returned unchanged; errors.Join exposes both causes only when both fail.
The accepted count advances only after a complete record write. Partial writes retain their bytes but do not count; short writes without an error return io.ErrShortWrite.
The reader remains borrowed. Tests observe reader ownership, writer close counts, record ordering, empty records, CRLF normalization and final unterminated records.

CLI parses the optional positional limit before opening files. Invalid usage exits 2; I/O/finalization errors exit 1 on stderr; successful invocations produce no stdout or stderr. Returning through run lets input cleanup execute before os.Exit.

Built-executable tests verify legacy unlimited calls, zero/positive bounds, dash-prefixed positional paths, malformed/negative/overflowing limits, missing input, output-open failure and an accepted prefix after scanner failure.
README documents build/run commands, library calls, ownership, errors, exit codes and partial-output behavior.
Only the supplied module and this report were changed; no commits, installations or external actions were performed.
material_limits: Verification used installed Go 1.26.5 on darwin/arm64. The module remains at Go 1.22 and uses APIs available by that version; Go 1.22 itself was not executed.
staticcheck is not installed, as confirmed by which returning exit 1; no installation was attempted.
Writer Close failures are deterministic library fixtures. A real filesystem Close failure was not induced through the CLI.
Existing bufio.Scanner token-size limits and input read-ahead remain. Output publication is not atomic; accepted or partial bytes can remain on failure.
